attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use an explicit exponential lower bound for general Resolution against the promise of polynomially many CDCL conflicts and a resolution trace.
attacks.method: Expand each first-UIP conflict analysis into its polynomial-size Resolution derivation. Polynomially many conflicts on an N-variable input then yield a polynomial-size Resolution refutation. Apply an explicit bounded-degree expander Tseitin family with exponential general-Resolution size lower bounds.
attacks.notes: The contradiction uses only unsatisfiable inputs. Branching, restarts, deletion, and polynomial memory cannot bypass a lower bound on the final Resolution trace.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Rescue H048 by choosing a more sophisticated fixed policy.
attacks.method: Observe that the lower bound applies to every Resolution refutation, not merely to one branching or restart policy. Any standard CDCL run producing a Resolution trace is covered.
attacks.notes: Changing the policy cannot defeat proof-system size lower bounds while the logged proof system remains Resolution.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Check whether H054 really needs policy-by-policy diagonalization.
attacks.method: Use the same explicit Resolution-hard Tseitin family for every fixed standard CDCL policy. A polynomial-conflict run would expand to a polynomial Resolution proof, contradicting the lower bound.
attacks.notes: This establishes a stronger policy-independent reduction under the exact standard CDCL and proof-logging assumptions, but the registry does not promote H054 to PROVED without formal and independent verification.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Evade the lower bound with polynomial preprocessing and proof logging.
attacks.method: If every preprocessing step has a polynomial Resolution derivation back to the original formula, append that derivation to any short refutation of the preprocessed formula. The original Resolution lower bound then still applies.
attacks.notes: Unlogged stronger preprocessing may leave the Resolution model and requires a new hypothesis; proof-preserving preprocessing does not rescue H048.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Find a certificate type that does not force disagreement with SAT.
attacks.method: Check each case: a witnessed satisfying assignment contradicts output 0; a fully restricted syntactically false formula contradicts output 1; and Shannon identity SAT(G)=SAT(G_0) OR SAT(G_1) makes any circuit-output inconsistency certify at least one error.
attacks.notes: The certificate language is sound under a canonical restriction and padding convention.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Expose H060 as merely renaming the desired SAT circuit lower bound.
attacks.method: Separate the proved local-error localization lemma from the unproved uniform constructor E. If C is correct, no certificate exists; constructing one for every C is therefore genuinely the hard diagonalization step.
attacks.notes: H060 is not an easier theorem by definition, but it replaces coNP-style negative certificates with a local, checkable target suitable for range-avoidance reductions.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that finite H041 interface gates cannot be compiled to AND/OR DNNF without exponential expansion.
attacks.method: Audit whether every fixed finite Boolean gate can be replaced by a constant-size deterministic decomposable circuit under the proposed support typing. Arbitrary gates may require case splitting, but the gate set is finite and fan-in bounded.
attacks.notes: The typing discipline must include a certified constant-size expansion table for each allowed gate; this is a concrete formalization obligation.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Find a DNNF-hard family with a fully DNNF-safe polynomial elimination run.
attacks.method: Assume the compilation induction and compare with the explicit DNNF lower-bound family. Such a run would immediately contradict the lower bound, so any counterexample must invalidate the induction or the typing premise.
attacks.notes: No valid typed run defeating the known lower bound was found.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use affine substitutions to collapse the non-affine expander gadget.
attacks.method: Test the statement against pure Tseitin systems and gadgets whose variables become identified under low-rank substitutions. Pure parity cores fail as witnesses, which is why H062 explicitly requires a substitution-stable non-affine coupling.
attacks.notes: The attack identifies the main construction constraint but no universal collapse theorem.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Rely only on a random gadget and call the family explicit.
attacks.method: Require deterministic polynomial-time construction and a proof of expansion after every allowed affine substitution, not merely high probability over an uncommitted random choice.
attacks.notes: H062 survives as a target but its next gate is an explicit pseudorandom construction, not a random-CNF existence argument.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Reuse the decisive H048 attack against parity-enhanced CDCL.
attacks.method: Compare proof systems. H063 may branch on arbitrary affine equations and logs Res(XOR), so a lower bound against ordinary Resolution does not cover the generated proof trace.
attacks.notes: H063 was created precisely by changing the proof system rather than changing only the policy.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Apply bounded-depth or restricted Res(XOR) lower bounds to the unrestricted policy.
attacks.method: Check the depth, regularity, and rule restrictions of known lower bounds against unrestricted dag-like linear-clause learning with restarts.
attacks.notes: Existing restricted lower bounds motivate H064 but do not settle the exact unrestricted solver model.
